problem: Research ticket asking whether proxy modules can intercept what actually gets sent to NetSuite, or whether they are limited to capturing user input. The ns-gm RESTlet uses a dynamic module injection pattern (new Function(...moduleNames, userCode)) that makes proxy substitution architecturally viable. Prior research (tickets cmnqr8lkk and cmnrx64kr) has already established Approach B (Two-Phase RESTlet with Module Proxy) as the recommended path.

files.why: The deployed NetSuite RESTlet. Lines 7-16: AMD define() loads 24 N/* modules. Lines 71-96: moduleMap object maps short names to real module references. Lines 115-125: dynamic moduleParamNames/moduleParamValues arrays built from requestedModules — this is the proxy substitution point. Lines 163-169: safeExecute() creates function via new Function(...moduleNames, userCode) and calls it with ...moduleValues. This is the core mechanism that enables proxy module interception.
Express proxy with /run (lines 35-86) and /logs (lines 88-128) endpoints. Forwards requests to RESTlet via nsapi.REST.post(). New /dry-run and /execute endpoints would follow this pattern.
OAuth 2.0 M2M JWT auth. nsapi.REST.post() handles token acquisition/caching, retry on 401. All new endpoints reuse this.
v1.0.5, Node >=24. Dependencies: axios, commander, express, jose. No test framework, no lint/typecheck scripts in package.json.
CLI run command. Posts code to proxy /run endpoint. Backward compatibility boundary — must remain unchanged.
CLI entry point via Commander. All command registrations.

facts: The RESTlet's module injection pattern (new Function(...moduleNames, userCode) at line 166, called with ...moduleValues at line 169) enables proxy substitution by replacing entries in the moduleParamValues array before execution.

The moduleMap at lines 71-96 contains 24 pre-loaded N/* modules: log, search, record, runtime, format, query, transaction, file, https, http, email, error, url, encode, crypto, currency, render, xml, config, task, redirect, cache, certificateControl, workflow.

The moduleParamNames/moduleParamValues arrays (lines 115-125) are built dynamically from requestedModules via loadModule(). For dry-run, the 'record' entry can be replaced with a proxy wrapper object before being passed to safeExecute().

User code receives modules as positional function parameters — it calls record.load(), record.save(), etc. without knowing whether these are real or proxied objects. This is the key answer to 'can we hijack what gets sent': YES, by swapping the module object the code receives.

Proxy modules do NOT just capture user input. Read operations (load, getFields, copy) pass through to real N/record module. Write operations (save, submitFields, delete) are intercepted to capture before/after state without committing.
Prior research ticket cmnqr8lkk recommends Approach B (Two-Phase RESTlet with Module Proxy) over Approach A (separate UserEventScript) due to governance chaining risk in beforeSubmit hooks.
Prior diagnosis ticket cmnrx64kr confirms proxy module viability with detailed before/after capture spec for load, save, create+save, submitFields, delete operations.
Current RESTlet action dispatcher (lines 23-37) handles only 'run' and 'getscriptexecutionlogs'. New actions ('dry-run', 'execute-approved') would be additive else-if branches.
SuiteScript 2.1 (@NApiVersion 2.1 at line 2) confirms modern JavaScript support including object spread, destructuring, closures needed for clean proxy implementation.
Production DB: 0 EXECUTE-mode tickets exist. 10 NsGmCredential records across organizations. TicketMode.EXECUTE is defined in Prisma schema but unused.
ns-gm has no test framework, no lint scripts, no typecheck scripts. Quality gates are limited to manual testing.
The helix-global-server has a duplicate copy of the RESTlet at netsuite-setup/FileCabinet/SuiteScripts/ns_gm_restlet.js deployed via SDF.
